findings.claim: Both suggested signatures omit the local coefficient-ring assumptions of their packet/source statements and are false. A surjective ring map to the residual field does not suffice to normalize a conjugator by a scalar unit. The trace signature lacks even surjectivity. The prose convention about residue fields does not add a Lean hypothesis.
findings.evidence: At Mathlib 082e2d3, Mathlib/RingTheory/LocalRing/Defs.lean:30-34 defines IsLocalRing as a separate predicate; GeneralLinearGroup/Defs.lean:43-45 and :188 identify GL with matrix units and its ring-map functor. Counterexample: A=Z, k=F5, pi mod 5, discrete topologies and G=S3. Let C=[0,-1;1,-1], S=[0,1;1,0], rho their six-element representation, a=[2,5;5,12] with det=-1 and a mod 5=2I, and rho'=a rho a^-1. The residual lifts agree and all traces agree. I,C,S,CS have flattened determinant -3, so the residual matrix-span hypothesis holds. Commuting with S and C forces an integral matrix to be scalar; the GL2(Z) centralizer is therefore {+I,-I}. Any conjugator from rho to rho' is +/-a, reducing to 2I or 3I, never I. Thus neither strict-conjugacy conclusion holds. Gee v2 Lemma 3.7, pp. 12-13, uses the local category of section 3.1; Kisin Lecture 1 Theorem 1.4.1, pp. 3-4, uses local-Artinian coefficients. Both source statements retain the assumptions the Lean signatures dropped.
findings.fix: Put both signatures on the coefficient categories imported from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1, with their genuine residue map and kernel identification, or state equivalent explicit local hypotheses matching each source theorem. Preserve the correctly scoped packet statements. Add this integral S3 example as a negative test and an allowed Artinian-local example testing scalar normalization; do not duplicate the coefficient category locally.

findings.where: research/blueprint/packets/GlobalGaloisDeformations.json: R04.3/relative-tangent-space and its ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.5 request; research/blueprint/readmes/GlobalGaloisDeformations.md: relative tangent-space paragraph
findings.claim: The statement specifies a cone using ordinary C•(G,ad0), but its proof needs Gee's modified complex with full ad in degree zero globally and at framed places. The displayed construction loses scalar changes of framing. The proof and the packet's corrected #T-1 formula are inconsistent with that construction. The reader separately still prints the old #T constant despite the already recorded E3 correction.
findings.evidence: Gee v2 section 3.23, p. 16, explicitly says 'Let C⁰₀(G, ad⁰ρ̄) := C⁰(G, ad ρ̄)' and uses trace-zero cochains only in positive global degree; local degree zero is the sum of full ad cochains at T. Its relative degree i is C₀^i plus C_loc^(i-1), with differential (d phi, res phi-d psi). Set F=Q, p=3, n=1, S=T={3,5}, residual character and fixed determinant both 1. All representation lifts are forced to be 1, but framed deformations are (1+m_A)^2/diagonal(1+m_A), naturally 1+m_A by the ratio of frames. Thus Rloc=O, Rglobal framed=O[[X]], and relative tangent dimension is 1. Since ad0=0, ordinary trace-zero cochains give dimension 0; retaining only local full-ad degree zero gives 2, still wrong. The correct complex gives k^2/diag(k). The reader's #T formula also gives 2; the packet's E3-corrected formula gives 1. R02.5 and SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2's actual nodes do not already specify this modified framed complex.
findings.fix: Specify Gee's modified degree-zero global and local terms, all remaining local terms, the mapping-fibre shift and differential. Tighten the existing R02.5 request to this exact interface, using the existing Selmer/cohomology owners. Distinguish the dual ordinary Selmer kernel from the framed complex. Preserve #T-1 in the packet and propagate its existing E3 correction into the reader. Add rank-one tests with two framings, one framing and no framings; the two-framing test must give k^2/diag(k), dimension 1.

findings.where: research/blueprint/packets/GlobalGaloisDeformations.json: R04.5/odd-taylor-wiles-primes proofSteps[2], acceptance[2] and Taylor citation; corresponding reader spanning argument
findings.claim: The common proof uses irreducibility of ad0(rhobar)(1) under either source's hypothesis. Cyclotomic absolute irreducibility in the KW branch does not imply adjoint irreducibility; permitted dihedral images have a proper invariant adjoint line. Consequently Gee's whole-adjoint spanning step leaves the KW branch unproved. The cited Taylor title is also wrong: KW invokes the meromorphic-continuation paper, not Remarks on a conjecture of Fontaine and Mazur.
findings.evidence: Take p=5, F=Q, K the splitting field of X^3-2, Gal(K/Q)=S3, and the standard C,S representation from finding /1 modulo 5 (over F25 if all eigenvalues are required). Its residual span is M2, and K intersects Q(zeta5) trivially: K's quadratic subfield is Q(sqrt(-3)), whereas Q(zeta5)'s is Q(sqrt(5)). Thus the cyclotomic restriction is absolutely irreducible. It is totally odd. But J=C-C^-1=[1,-2;2,-1] spans a proper trace-zero invariant line, with CJC^-1=J and SJS^-1=-J; the Tate twist preserves it. Gee v2 p. 39 justifies irreducibility 'since the image of ρ contains SL2(Fp)', the stronger alternative. KW II author-final Lemmas 5.2-5.3, pp. 47-48, cite [59]; bibliography p. 97 identifies Taylor, On the meromorphic continuation of degree two L-functions. Taylor Lemma 2.5, printed pp. 749-750, requires detection separately on an irreducible constituent V and explicitly treats 'If dim W = 1' and the dimension-two complement case. The correct KW prime-existence conclusion is not refuted; the proposed proof's unsupported assertion is.
findings.fix: Separate the source-specific detecting-element lemmas: use Gee's irreducible-adjoint argument only with its SL2-image hypothesis; for KW request the constituent-detection statement, including its induced/dihedral cases, from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4, keeping R02.6's H1 vanishing separate. Add the allowed S3/dihedral example as a regression test, without strengthening the KW theorem to exclude it.
